feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with clear positioning, credible public-sector experience, and good evidence of progression and scope. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness and impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo from coordinator to director, reinforcing credibility and growth.  
- Good scale indicators: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms add substance.  
- Broad but coherent profile: strategy, governance, analytics, CMS, multimedia, and AI-enabled search all align well with the target brand.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across Header, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; several themes/tools appear multiple times. Consolidating would improve focus and save space.  
- Add more outcome-driven results beyond activity descriptions, especially in freelance/current role and earlier NACo roles; quantify improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or campaign performance where possible.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation in bullets is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)” instead. No major misspellings or grammar errors otherwise.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant positioning with a clear public-sector digital leadership focus. However, it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and foreground the most credible differentiators: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct, executive language such as “leading” or “delivering” to strengthen authority.
- Consider a rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Builds scalable editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences that improve discovery, coordination, and audience engagement.”
- Standardize style: use either “AI-enabled” consistently across the CV and consider “public-sector organizations” over “complex, mission-driven organizations” for specificity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely echoes the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on differentiating strengths rather than restating broad areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more consistent noun phrases; avoid mixing “operations,” “systems,” and “experiences” unevenly.
- Prioritize the strongest, most marketable areas first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search, automation.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space allows, replace “Multi-channel communications operations” with a more distinctive phrase like “Cross-channel content operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” overlaps with Header, Recent Projects, and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” and several other items duplicate Topline Skills almost directly.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tighten phrasing, standardize style, and emphasize what is distinct or especially current.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” to reinforce recency and separate this from core experience.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: “Designed…,” “Built…,” “Developed…,” “Launched…” and trim stacked nouns.
- Make outcomes more concrete where possible; e.g., note user benefit, campaign purpose, or scale without repeating role bullets.
- Standardize style: spell out “10 x 20-foot,” keep capitalization consistent, and consider “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” once only.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI Hybrid Search” overlaps with the current freelance role; keep this footer version shorter and more project-focused.
- “Advocacy Video Series” and parts of the anniversary campaign repeat NACo multimedia achievements already described in Work Experience.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope and good technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact outcomes and add scale/results to distinguish it from your NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal campaign delivery, content operations, and enterprise web improvements.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one outcome-focused line: “Built cross-channel workflows, governance standards, and analytics systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more results-oriented: mention number of sites/pages, users, campaign launches, turnaround time, or stakeholder groups supported.
- Recast the AI bullet as a flagship achievement: “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content modeling, and user discovery experience.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “enterprise web improvement” overlap with the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize what is new here (consulting scope, AI search, campaign builds).
- The footer project examples already cover microsites and AI search, so avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Combine web modernization into one impact bullet: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based; add metrics if available: email growth/open rates, social engagement, video output, event reach, cost savings, or production turnaround.
- Tighten ops/analytics bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version focused on enterprise oversight and results.
- Video/programming language also echoes older NACo entries; emphasize studio buildout and organizational capacity, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item is too close to the adjacent NACo roles and reads as support-oriented rather than ownership-driven. Tighten it around scope, channel leadership, and systems/process impact.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and sharpen verbs: “Owned four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague process language with a clearer systems angle: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role and the footer project; keep focus here on scaling/owning it, not originating video broadly.
- “Publishing workflows” and “coordination” also appear in the Director role; avoid repeating governance language too heavily.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around leadership scope rather than repeating generic capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, differentiated terms: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise web and content strategy”; “Multi-channel communications leadership” → “Cross-channel digital operations leadership.”
- Add governance/operating-model language that signals seniority: “Editorial governance and publishing operations” is stronger than “Editorial systems and governance.”
- Tighten audience/messaging phrasing: “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” → “Public-sector, membership, and advocacy communications.”
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise web and content strategy
- Editorial governance and publishing operations
- Cross-channel digital operations leadership
- Public-sector, membership, and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content planning

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- Avoid repeating “multi-channel communications” here if it already appears elsewhere; “operations leadership” adds more value.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill mix, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize platform leadership and execution strengths tied to recent work, not repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization” instead of listing multiple CMSs first.
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, API/integration work, workflow automation, AI-enabled search.
- Trim lower-signal or older items here; move/leave detailed tools like jQuery, SharePoint, Power Pages, Airtable in “Technical + IT.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • AI-enabled search and structured content experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating full tool inventories in both places.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep wording tighter or vary it slightly.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic inventory. Tighten it to emphasize strategic analytics capability and avoid repeating the more detailed “Technical + IT” section.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” rather than only platform names.
- Use grouped wording for concision: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace weaker items with stronger business-facing language: change “Leadership reporting” to “executive dashboards and decision support.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and KPI design • Executive dashboards and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX insight and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let Technical + IT hold the full tool list.
- “Performance analysis” overlaps with broader analytics language; “performance optimization” is sharper and more outcome-oriented.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and older NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and make the phrasing more senior and specific.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, grouped phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Consider leading with the most marketable capability: “Hybrid and virtual event production” or “Livestream and studio production”
- If this section allows, add scope/context rather than task wording, e.g. “Broadcast-quality in-house studio production” instead of “Video production and editing”
- Keep to 3–4 bullets max; remove “editing” if covered by tools like Premiere Pro elsewhere

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same exact phrasing
- “Studio operations” and “Livestream studio workflows” are also echoed in Technical + IT, so this item should stay outcome-/capability-focused, not tool-focused

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” It should emphasize platform depth and recency—especially Drupal—rather than read like a duplicate tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level of use: **Drupal (enterprise modernization, microsites, structured content)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, prioritize by relevance/recency: put **Drupal** first and consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it’s not materially important to recent roles.
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** or **CMS Platforms** for tighter phrasing.
- If you want more impact, add qualifiers instead of just names: e.g., **Drupal 10**, **enterprise SharePoint**, **campaign microsites**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one as a concise platform list and the other focused on broader capabilities.
- Avoid repeating “CMS modernization” here since it already appears in Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually supporting recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for specificity and consistency: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • REST/API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions (CI/CD)”
- Drop version numbers unless they matter operationally; “HTML5/CSS3” feels dated and adds little value.
- Consider grouping by function for faster scanning: “Front-end: HTML/CSS, JavaScript/jQuery | Integration: REST/API integrations, GTM | DevOps/Edge: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “front-end implementation for Drupal” or “deployment automation,” rather than more tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid expanding this item into automation tools already covered in its own section.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more clearly framed around orchestration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/workflow:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If you’ve built meaningful automations, consider replacing one lower-value tool with scope language, e.g. **Airtable workflow systems • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if they support the workflow-systems positioning.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platforms to include, but this item is too bare and undersells a clear strength shown in recent roles: enterprise email operations and audience engagement. It should read as a capability area, not just a software list.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency and standardize naming: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief parentheticals to signal depth: **Higher Logic (newsletter operations, audience segmentation)** • **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys (campaign automation)** • **Mailchimp (email production)**
- If you have metrics tied to these tools, move them into recent NACo bullets instead of here; keep this section tool-focused and concise.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and NACo email/newsletter bullets; avoid adding generic phrases like “email strategy” here unless tied to platform use.
- Don’t repeat analytics/reporting language already covered under “Data, Analytics & Optimization.”

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, tighten it to platforms plus methods, and make the optimization angle more specific.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting**
- Replace **SEO** with **Google Search Console** or **SEO analysis** to make it more concrete and tool/skill-specific.
- Replace **Dashboarding** with **KPI reporting** or **executive dashboards**; “dashboarding” reads vague and informal.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recently evidenced tools first: **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping the broader category there and using this section for only hard tools/methods.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid adding generic terms here that don’t add new information.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Emphasize “firsts,” team-building, and concrete outputs, while trimming generic workflow language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: website refresh scale, livestream/event volume, video cadence, audience growth, or team support.
- Tighten phrasing and make contributions more active: “supported the creation” → “helped build”; “high-impact digital content” → specific formats and frequency.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; if kept here, distinguish this as launching or initially producing the series.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; use “helped establish early digital production processes” instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around concrete ownership and outputs, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Condense the rest into one supporting clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support research, member engagement and policy communications.”
- If possible, add one metric or output count: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, or audiences/stakeholders served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research/program support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid broad “policy work” phrasing unless you can specify the function or result.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic for a senior profile and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, and make the capabilities feel current and professional.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative & Production Tools**
